review_items.rationale: Reviewed the fixed v1 harness and plan, accepted C-prepare-vballot-preservation v1, and raw CheckRun e4f3fbd3c91a45959da21038728d7adc. The written duty is exact preservation of the producer-reported VBallot through valid same-version RPC transfer, not agreement or progress. S-recovery handlePrepare constructs VBallot from inst.vbal and handlePrepareReply uses it for highest-value-ballot selection; S-messages distinguishes it from Ballot. Thus the producer/consumer relation supplies the local requirement independently of the implementation discrepancy. The fixed oracle compares decoded.vballot with produced.expected_vballot for scenario/acceptor/replica/instance, with produced explicitly selected as admission_alias; VBallot is not a correlation key. In owner_1 the raw prerequisite has acceptor=2, replica=1, instance=0, Ballot=3, Status=2 and expected_vballot=1; the uniquely matched later result has the same identity/Ballot/Status but vballot=0. owner_0 separately has expected/observed 0 and Ballot=5. Both observations are complete and parsed without errors; tests_passed means diagnostics completed, while the property comparison is violated. Constructor adaptation was checked against S-init/S-members: N=3 F=1, empty bounded rows, -1 prefixes, Thrifty and Dreply true, volatile state and fixed peer order. startPhase1 generates an initial owner-ID PreAccept; emitted bytes reach the selected distinct acceptor and establish PREACCEPTED_EQ and vbal. A distinct coordinator generates a higher Prepare through startRecoveryForInstance; acceptor handles it and emits bytes via real SendMsg/Marshal. The helper uses the actual registered New()/Unmarshal path and checks complete byte consumption. Producer-state sampling is faithful because handlePrepare directly copies those fields without further mutation; no concurrent handlers/executor run. The driver does not inject a fabricated PrepareReply or substitute its compared VBallot. Buffer transport and serial delivery select valid local calls without requiring arbitrary reordering, dropping fields, or overriding protocol logic. The coordinator recovery trigger is invoked directly, not a witnessed executor timer; that is a boundary of this explicitly local valid-message codec obligation, not an asserted timed global history. Pending unselected messages do not affect this completed transfer. The full PrepareReply codec omits VBallot; fresh allocation leaves it at zero. Neither exact request Ballot preservation nor other payload checks reconstruct the distinct provenance field before the recovery consumer. Contrary observations and scope qualifications retained: The zero-ballot case satisfies the equality; the finding is not that every PrepareReply changes VBallot. Request Ballot, Status, Seq, commands and dependencies passed transport diagnostics; request-ballot matching remains a separate protection. Self PrepareReply construction does not cross this codec, so the experiment does not claim all recovery support is corrupted. These qualify the consequence and input scope but do not contradict the nonzero local witness.

formation.explanation: A proposal is batched into its receiving replica row and starts phase 1 with owner-ID ballot. Conflict indices establish Seq/Deps. Thrifty PreAccept reaches selected alive peers, whose reports are qualified by lastTriedBallot and phase status. The owner merges attributes and either fast commits under threshold/equality/initial-ballot conditions (with a small-cluster exception) or broadcasts Accept and commits after a majority count. Full Commit carries commands and attributes; receivers reject stale ballots and already established decisions. Default Dreply=true delays client response until dependency/SCC execution. Sender and receiver codecs, not just handler structs, are part of this relationship.

context.explanation: Authority is per row/instance. inst.bal guards incoming work; leader bookkeeping lastTriedBallot guards phase replies. Executor-driven recovery replaces local attempt bookkeeping while retaining proposals and stored value; generated ballots depend on ID/N and optionally maxRecvBallot under master-granted IsLeader. Prepare raises the promise and reports prior vbal/status/attributes. A slow quorum including the self report selects support using VBallot, then preserves a reported committed state, accepts retained support, or restarts phase 1. Prior committed instances with commands bypass recovery. No global revocation mechanism was found; stale work is handled by these local promise/status/phase checks, whose actual strength remains investigable.

connection.explanation: Recovery authority does not independently determine a new value: its consumer uses reported support provenance/status and attributes to decide which formation path is eligible. bal may rise while vbal and prior attributes remain in handlePrepare, separating promise from support. The local recovery entry instead updates both ballots before self reporting; remote replies cross a codec that omits VBallot. These discrepancies are unresolved premises of support preservation, not assumed agreement failures. Old phase replies face attempt/phase guards; established commit messages have status/ballot guards. Pending client proposals are retained across recovery and sometimes requeued after NOOP; consumption still requires complete committed dependencies.

formation.explanation: A proposal is batched into its receiving replica row and starts phase 1 with owner-ID ballot. Conflict indices establish Seq/Deps. Thrifty PreAccept reaches selected alive peers, whose reports are qualified by lastTriedBallot and phase status. The owner merges attributes and either fast commits under threshold/equality/initial-ballot conditions (with a small-cluster exception) or broadcasts Accept and commits after a majority count. Full Commit carries commands and attributes; receivers reject stale ballots and already established decisions. Default Dreply=true delays client response until dependency/SCC execution. Sender and receiver codecs, not just handler structs, are part of this relationship.

context.explanation: Authority is per row/instance. inst.bal guards incoming work; leader bookkeeping lastTriedBallot guards phase replies. Executor-driven recovery replaces local attempt bookkeeping while retaining proposals and stored value; generated ballots depend on ID/N and optionally maxRecvBallot under master-granted IsLeader. Prepare raises the promise and reports prior vbal/status/attributes. A slow quorum including the self report selects support using VBallot, then preserves a reported committed state, accepts retained support, or restarts phase 1. Prior committed instances with commands bypass recovery. No global revocation mechanism was found; stale work is handled by these local promise/status/phase checks, whose actual strength remains investigable.

connection.explanation: Recovery authority does not independently determine a new value: its consumer uses reported support provenance/status and attributes to decide which formation path is eligible. bal may rise while vbal and prior attributes remain in handlePrepare, separating promise from support. The local recovery entry instead updates both ballots before self reporting; remote replies cross a codec that omits VBallot. These discrepancies are unresolved premises of support preservation, not assumed agreement failures. Old phase replies face attempt/phase guards; established commit messages have status/ballot guards. Pending client proposals are retained across recovery and sometimes requeued after NOOP; consumption still requires complete committed dependencies.

items.rationale: Reviewed the fixed v1 harness and plan, accepted C-prepare-vballot-preservation v1, and raw CheckRun e4f3fbd3c91a45959da21038728d7adc. The written duty is exact preservation of the producer-reported VBallot through valid same-version RPC transfer, not agreement or progress. S-recovery handlePrepare constructs VBallot from inst.vbal and handlePrepareReply uses it for highest-value-ballot selection; S-messages distinguishes it from Ballot. Thus the producer/consumer relation supplies the local requirement independently of the implementation discrepancy. The fixed oracle compares decoded.vballot with produced.expected_vballot for scenario/acceptor/replica/instance, with produced explicitly selected as admission_alias; VBallot is not a correlation key. In owner_1 the raw prerequisite has acceptor=2, replica=1, instance=0, Ballot=3, Status=2 and expected_vballot=1; the uniquely matched later result has the same identity/Ballot/Status but vballot=0. owner_0 separately has expected/observed 0 and Ballot=5. Both observations are complete and parsed without errors; tests_passed means diagnostics completed, while the property comparison is violated. Constructor adaptation was checked against S-init/S-members: N=3 F=1, empty bounded rows, -1 prefixes, Thrifty and Dreply true, volatile state and fixed peer order. startPhase1 generates an initial owner-ID PreAccept; emitted bytes reach the selected distinct acceptor and establish PREACCEPTED_EQ and vbal. A distinct coordinator generates a higher Prepare through startRecoveryForInstance; acceptor handles it and emits bytes via real SendMsg/Marshal. The helper uses the actual registered New()/Unmarshal path and checks complete byte consumption. Producer-state sampling is faithful because handlePrepare directly copies those fields without further mutation; no concurrent handlers/executor run. The driver does not inject a fabricated PrepareReply or substitute its compared VBallot. Buffer transport and serial delivery select valid local calls without requiring arbitrary reordering, dropping fields, or overriding protocol logic. The coordinator recovery trigger is invoked directly, not a witnessed executor timer; that is a boundary of this explicitly local valid-message codec obligation, not an asserted timed global history. Pending unselected messages do not affect this completed transfer. The full PrepareReply codec omits VBallot; fresh allocation leaves it at zero. Neither exact request Ballot preservation nor other payload checks reconstruct the distinct provenance field before the recovery consumer. Contrary observations and scope qualifications retained: The zero-ballot case satisfies the equality; the finding is not that every PrepareReply changes VBallot. Request Ballot, Status, Seq, commands and dependencies passed transport diagnostics; request-ballot matching remains a separate protection. Self PrepareReply construction does not cross this codec, so the experiment does not claim all recovery support is corrupted. These qualify the consequence and input scope but do not contradict the nonzero local witness.
